title: Kernel prioritizer for split-precision prefill and decode scheduling
creator: Priya Desai
description: Problem: Our current strategy picks an INT8 or FP8 execution path at model load time or per-layer static mapping, causing suboptimal latency and extra dequant/quant transitions during mixed-precision runs. For workloads with short golden prefixes (chat messages, short completions) the dequant overhead and stream synchronization for switching precision dominates tail latency. Goal: Implement a Kernel Prioritizer that chooses kernel implementation at request-time using runtime signals (sequence length, KV cache hit rate, layer sensitivity map) and schedules prefill vs decode stages to minimize p95 latency while preserving token throughput and accuracy targets.
design_decisions: 1) Decision to prefer late-path selection: compute candidate kernels early but defer final dispatch until microbatch boundaries to allow batching and KV cache alignment. 2) Use a layered sensitivity table derived from offline per-layer L2 norm and quantization noise tests to prefer FP8 on the top N attention blocks. 3) Introduce a dequant-skip heuristic: when the next stage is decode and the KV cache will reuse quantized keys, avoid dequant+requant if it increases GPU-to-GPU sync. 4) Prioritizer exposes per-request hints (latency_slo_ms, quality_budget) so that low-latency requests can bias toward FP8 fast path or hybrid with fewer dequant ops.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Risk: Additional branching at dispatch cost may add overhead; mitigated by caching selection per (model, seq_len_bucket, route).
- Tradeoff between accuracy and latency: lowering precision on sensitive layers can cause small output regressions; we bound this with quality_budget and can fallback to FP32/FP8 if eval thresholds fail.
- Complexity: new code touches scheduling and kernel registry; increased test surface and chance of regressions in lifecycle (rollouts).
experiments_and_metrics:
Summary of microbenchmarks on V100/RTX8000-equivalent nodes with Llama-like 70B: 
- Baseline (static mapping): decode p95 142ms, p50 38ms, tokens/s 850.
- Kernel Prioritizer prototype (static sensitivity + late selection): decode p95 98ms (-31%), p50 36ms (-5%), tokens/s 820 (-3.5%).
- With dequant-skip heuristic enabled: decode p95 85ms (-40%), p50 35ms, tokens/s 810.
- Weighted accuracy delta (avg token-level KL on eval set): +0.8% vs baseline when allowing TOP-3 layer FP8.
Notes: improvements concentrated on short sequences (<64). For long sequences improvements are smaller but resource usage reduced due to better batching alignment.
implementation_notes:
- New components: kernel_prioritizer.cc/.h, priority_cache LRU keyed by (model_id, seq_bucket, route_hint), sensitivity_loader (json manifest generated by offline eval).
- Integration points: runtime dispatcher (before kernel selection), prefill scheduler (to group requests by precision affinity), and kernel registry (add metadata flags: supports_int8, supports_fp8, dequant_cost_est).
- GPU work reordering: use CUDA streams per-precision lane to allow overlap of int8 and fp8 compute; ensure KV cache writes use unified stream ordering to keep correctness.
- Telemetry: expose token-level counters for path chosen, dequant ops skipped, and per-request latency breakouts.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for prioritizer decision logic with deterministic sensitivity tables.
2) Integration tests on CI small-GPU instance with both INT8 and FP8 kernels enabled; verify outputs within quality_budget for random seeds.
3) Staging perf test ramp with A/B: 10% traffic for 48h measuring p50/p95, throughput, and error rates.
4) Chaos test: simulate a kernel failure on INT8 path to exercise automatic fallback and measure degradation.
5) Long-run stability: 7-day soak with mixed workloads (chat, summarize, codegen).
acceptance_criteria:
- p95 latency reduction >= 25% for short-seq (<64) decode compared to baseline on our standard perf job.
- Token-throughput degradation <= 5%.
- Evaluations: quality delta <= 1.5% on held-out eval prompts when using default sensitivity table.
- No segfaults or correctness failures in 7-day soak.
- Monitoring dashboards: prioritizer path adoption, dequant-skip rate, and fallback counts visible in console.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Internal canary on dedicated capacity (runtime-1.19-canary) with 0 traffic routing changes — use synthetic load. Phase 2: 5% real traffic for non-critical tenants for 72h. Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 50% with auto-rollout pause on error budget breach. Final: enable by default for runtime-1.19 if metrics stable.
Fallback: simple env flag to force static mapping and a circuit breaker on error budget to disable prioritizer across a region.
